title: Lumbar Spine MRI
raw_html:
LCD L33822 (v11): Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Lumbar Spine

Coverage Indications

Under version 11 prior to the 2022 revision, lumbar spine MRI required at least 4 weeks of documented conservative therapy for uncomplicated low back pain or radiculopathy before imaging.

Red Flag Exceptions

Immediate lumbar spine MRI without prior conservative management is covered when cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor deficit, or suspected spinal infection is documented.

title: Lumbar Spine MRI
raw_html:
LCD L33822: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Lumbar Spine

Coverage Indications

Lumbar spine MRI is considered medically reasonable and necessary for patients with persistent radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, or severe low back pain that fails to respond to at least 6 weeks of documented conservative therapy.

Clinical ScenarioConservative Therapy RequiredCovered Modality
Uncomplicated RadiculopathyMinimum 6 weeks physical therapy or medicationMRI lumbar spine without contrast (72148)
Cauda Equina Syndrome (Red Flag)Immediate imaging; no waiting periodUrgent MRI lumbar spine without contrast (72148)
Suspected Spinal Infection or Post-Op ScarNo waiting period for red flagsMRI without and with contrast (72158)

Red Flag Exceptions

Immediate lumbar spine MRI without prior conservative management is covered when red flag signs are documented: progressive motor deficit, saddle anesthesia, bowel or bladder incontinence, suspected malignancy, or epidural abscess.

title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for Obstructive Sleep Apnea
raw_html:
LCD L33718: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

Initial 12-Week Coverage Criteria

A single-level CPAP device (E0601) is covered for an initial 12-week trial when a beneficiary has a face-to-face clinical evaluation and a facility or home sleep test confirming obstructive sleep apnea.

OSA Diagnostic ThresholdRequired ComorbiditiesInitial Trial Period
AHI or RDI >= 15 events/hourNone required12 weeks (90 days)
AHI or RDI 5 to 14 events/hourExcessive daytime sleepiness, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or stroke12 weeks (90 days)

Continued Coverage After 90 Days

Continued PAP coverage beyond the first 3 months requires a clinical re-evaluation between days 31 and 91 demonstrating symptom improvement and objective adherence of at least 4 hours per night on 70 percent of nights during a consecutive 30-day period.

title: Cataract Extraction (Including Complex Cataract Surgery)
raw_html:
LCD L35041: Cataract Extraction (Including Complex Cataract Surgery)

Medical Necessity Criteria

Cataract extraction with intraocular lens implantation is covered when lens opacity causes functional impairment in activities of daily living such as driving, reading, or recognizing faces, and visual symptoms cannot be corrected with eyeglasses.

Procedure TypeCPT CodeQualifying Criteria
Standard Cataract Extraction66984Functional impairment in ADLs plus best-corrected visual acuity interference
Complex Cataract Extraction66982Miotic pupil requiring iris expansion device, mature white cataract, or capsular tension ring

Second Eye Surgery

Cataract surgery on the second eye is covered when the patient continues to experience functional visual disability after first-eye stabilization or symptomatic anisometropia.

title: MolDX: Molecular Diagnostic Tests for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
raw_html:
LCD L34998: MolDX Molecular Diagnostic Tests for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

Covered Biomarker Testing

Next-generation sequencing (NGS) and targeted single-gene molecular assays are covered for Medicare beneficiaries with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to identify actionable driver mutations guiding FDA-approved targeted therapies.

Biomarker TargetPrimary CPT CodeTherapeutic Actionability
EGFR Exon 19 / L858R81235EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor selection
Targeted Solid Tumor NGS Panel (5-50 genes)81445Concurrent EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS G12C, RET evaluation

Repeat Testing Limitations

Repeat molecular profiling is limited to disease progression on targeted therapy when resistance mutations such as EGFR T790M would alter clinical management.
